moments.text: Five rows, one per model. Every row plays the same change: rename two fields.
Every model starts from a written intent.
Then each one writes requirements, or a spec.
Watch the purple boxes. That is where the architecture rule lives.
In every model, the rule is something the agent reads.
The work is broken into tasks.
The agent writes the code. In every row, it drops the old names.
Review. Where a model has one, it is advice. It does not block.
Now CI. Only the last row has an architecture check.
Red. Rule ARCH-4 blocks the merge.
The agent fixes the code, and CI passes.
Release: a person says yes. The other teams keep working.
The rule is written down in every model.
What differs: does something check the rule after the code is written?
